designChallenge: Explicit motion-led creative brief using the same commerce requirements as clothing-shop. Compare only within this brief and frozen protocol; retain the ordinary shop as a separate usability task.
prompt: Build a distinctive, motion-led ecommerce experience for this fictional clothing label. I want ambitious art direction and perceptible continuity as I scroll, including authored image framing and a transition that carries the visual idea into the shopping experience. It must feel good in motion, not only in a screenshot. Source or create coherent, representative clothing imagery; do not imply those images are verified photographs of this fictional inventory. Consider video, pixelation, parallax, or a spatial treatment where they strengthen your concept, and choose the approach rather than adding every effect. Briefly compare two materially different creative treatments, choose the strongest autonomously, and build one faithful prototype slice with its entry and exit before completing the route. Nobody is available to answer during the build. Preserve the practical shopping flow: seeing garments, checking sizes, filtering, and using the bag on desktop and touch mobile. Test normal motion and reduced motion separately. A successful result should be memorable and coherent beyond the hero while remaining easy to buy from.

preserve: All nine garments with their exact names, categories, prices, colour lists, fabric statements, and detail sentences

The per-garment sold-out sizes, which cannot be added to the bag: XS on the Oxford Shirt, S and XL on the Chore Jacket, M on the Pleated Trouser, L on the Lambswool Crew, XS and S on the Shawl Cardigan, XL on the Camp Short
The category filter, including its counts and the All state
Choosing a size before adding to the bag, and the bag itself, which must name each line's garment, size, and price, allow a line to be removed, and show a running subtotal
The delivery thresholds and the amount still needed to reach free delivery over £100
The full size chart — every size row with its chest, waist, and sleeve measurement in centimetres — and the between-sizes advice
Every care fact, including which garments cannot be machine washed, that nothing goes in a tumble dryer, that the denim is unwashed and will bleed, and the repair offer
The shipping and returns statement for all three regions, the 60 day return window, and the same-day exchange
All three customer reviews with their names and what they bought
The three shop facts: eleven people and one shop in Leeds, four named factories, and that there are never any sales
